title: Zone-aware egress NAT with assigned EIP pools and security-group hardening
author: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Context: Private deployments in multi-AZ environments need predictable egress IPs for allowlisting and per-AZ capacity isolation. The current installer uses a single shared NAT layer which makes IP allowlisting brittle and complicates egress budgeting across availability zones. This PR introduces zone-aware NAT gateway provisioning with deterministic allocation from configurable EIP pools and tightens control-plane security groups for the control-plane-to-worker and control-plane-egress flows.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new terraform module and variables to allocate per-az NAT gateways backed by pre-allocated EIP pools; introduces an optional deterministic allocation map so customers can pin EIPs to AZs; updates Helm templates used by the private control plane to surface NAT/EIP configuration and new annotations for kube-proxy egress routing; hardens default security-group rules by converting wide 0.0.0.0/0 control-plane egress to scoped destination CIDRs and explicit port lists; provides an opt-out flag for customers who prefer a single shared egress or who manage NAT externally.

Key implementation notes: deterministic_eip_map (map string->list) is a user-provided mapping of AZ->EIP list used in the tf module; when not provided, the module will allocate from an EIP pool per-AZ with deterministic naming so re-runs are idempotent. NAT Gateway resources are created per-AZ with route table attachments isolated to control-plane subnets only. Security-group changes are additive by default (creates redwood-controlplane-tight and migrates rules gradually). The module exports a small status object (id list) via Terraform outputs used by the Helm chart templates.

Compatibility and rollout: this change is non-breaking by default. The migration path for existing clusters is a two-step upgrade: 1) enable the module in dry-run mode to generate recommended eip allocations and preview Terraform plan; 2) switch on create_nat_per_az=true and apply. A migration helper script (scripts/migrate-egress.sh) is included to validate connectivity, rotate NAT attachments, and perform rollback if healthchecks fail. The opt-out flag (controlplane.egress.use_shared_nat=false by default for upgrades) lets operators defer migration.

Testing: Terraform unit runs were executed against a local terraform-compliance harness and integration tests were run in the benchmark-lab AWS account with a 3-AZ topology. Smoke tests include IP allowlist verification for a sample webhook (external firewall), e2e service-to-internet flows, and failover tests where a single AZ NAT is destroyed to validate fallback to neighboring AZ NATs if enabled. CI summary below.

Rollout notes for SRE and customer-ops: 1) For customers with static allowlist requirements we recommend providing deterministic_eip_map during install. 2) For existing clusters on older installer versions, follow the migrate-egress.sh workflow and schedule a maintenance window to apply Terraform state changes to route tables. 3) If using marketplace images with strict IP ACLs coordinate with network teams to pre-provision EIPs.

Related: builds on work from ENG-4020 (subnet allocation) and complements INF-71 (privatelink egress proxy).

review_conversation: Liam Chen: Can we make the default behavior opt-in for new installs? I don't want surprises for single-AZ customers.

Maya Rodriguez: Default for new installs is per-az NAT true; I added 'create_nat_per_az' and documented the opt-out flag. For single-AZ installs the module short-circuits to single NAT so behavior is safe.
Sofia Kaplan: Security changes look good but we need a short window of overlap where both SGs exist to avoid breaking existing control plane connections.

Maya Rodriguez: Added sg migration plan and a tf resource 'redwood_controlplane_sg_migration' as a no-op resource that operators can plan/apply before switching rules. See security/sg-migrations/README.
Ravi Desai: Tested migration script in benchmark-lab. Recommend adding a metric for nat_gw_active_count to observability-pack.
Maya Rodriguez: Added metric export and a dashboard JSON in observability-pack under separate PR (linked).
Sofia Kaplan: Approving pending one small comment on variable naming consistency.
Maya Rodriguez: Addressed naming comment and squashed commits. Ready to merge.
release_notes: Add optional per-AZ NAT gateways with configurable EIP pools for predictable egress IPs; introduce deterministic_eip_map for pinning EIPs to AZs; tighten control-plane security groups and provide a migration helper script. Non-breaking by default; follow migration guide for existing clusters.
manual_steps: 1) Review example.tfvars and generate deterministic_eip_map if allowlisting is required. 2) Run scripts/migrate-egress.sh in a staging environment. 3) Apply Terraform plan during maintenance window. 4) Validate external webhook connectivity and monitor nat_gw_active_count metric.
notes: This PR requires AWS account permissions to allocate EIPs and create NAT gateways. Customers using BYO-NAT should set controlplane.egress.use_shared_nat=true and skip providing deterministic_eip_map.
